convention: anthropics/skills/skill-creator evals.json — two kinds, per references/schemas.md. `kind:"trigger"` fixtures carry `should_trigger` so skill-creator's description-optimisation loop can score train/held-out trigger accuracy. `kind:"behavioural"` fixtures carry `expectations[]` asserting the skill's execution contract (SKILL.md cardinal rules 2, 4 and 5) holds on a described v1 project — graded against the transcript, not a codemod.
notes: Trigger positives target v1->v2 migration prompts: explicit phrasing OR any v1 surface mention (re-frame.db, dispatch-with, reg-global-interceptor, reg-sub-raw, ^:flush-dom, re-frame.alpha, re-frame-test, old top-level :dispatch / :dispatch-n effect-map keys) OR a v1 add-on-lib fingerprint (http-fx / :http-xhrio, async-flow-fx / :async-flow). Trigger negatives target greenfield, authoring on already-v2, live-runtime, and pure spec / EP questions. The five behavioural fixtures (20-24) grade the outcome of one explicit migration request end to end: a Type-A-only migration proceeds through the project's own compile/test gates without a paste loop; a mixed Type-A/Type-B migration runs the safe work and pauses ONCE, on the batched semantic decisions; no false completion is claimed when the interactive boot smoke has no runtime to drive; the M-70 x M-73 interceptor-chain composition holds — standard path chains land as [:rf.interceptor/path <path>] metadata refs (never a surviving inline (rf/path ...) call or positional vector, both hard v2 registration errors) while a custom inline interceptor is held as an unresolved M-70 Type-B decision rather than claimed migrated (rf2-8odvg); and M-42's dom-node half is swept on the CLASSIC BRIDGE, not deferred to slim (rf2-6r9j.37) — stock Reagent 2.0.1 has already deleted reagent.dom/dom-node, so a bridge-targeted (rdom/dom-node this) breaks the build and the site must be reported before the first compile. Their prompts describe the project in words (no fixture tree) so the grader reads the agent's plan, tool calls and report rather than a diff.

evals.name: behav-type-a-only-runs-gates-no-paste-loop
evals.prompt: Migrate this project from re-frame v1 to re-frame2. It is a small Reagent app on deps.edn + shadow-cljs: deps.edn pins re-frame/re-frame 1.4.3 and declares a :test alias; package.json has `test` (the shadow-cljs :test build) and `build` scripts; every handler is reg-event-db / reg-event-fx and several return {:db ... :dispatch [...]}. No reg-sub-raw, no interceptors, no add-on libraries, React is already 19. The re-frame2 corpus is at ../re-frame2 pinned to <sha>; target version <v2-version>. Go.
expectations: Runs Phase 0a (inventory-and-plan) and Phase 0b (the floor gate) BEFORE any dep edit, then applies M-0 and the Type-A rules the description implies (M-73 reg-event-db / reg-event-fx -> reg-event; M-8 top-level :dispatch -> :fx), each with a sweep-level announcement (rule id, matched file count, representative diff) — and PROCEEDS after announcing; it does not stop to ask whether it may continue (cardinal rule 4).

After the dep swap it RUNS the project's own install and compile / test commands, discovered from deps.edn and package.json (`npm install`, `clojure -M:test`, `npm test` / `npx shadow-cljs compile test`), through Bash, and reads the results — it never prints a command for the user to run and paste back (cardinal rule 5).
Runs only what the project declares: no invented gate, nothing destructive or deploy-shaped, no unrelated dependency bumps.
The Phase-6 report's Verification line quotes the exact commands it ran and their observed results (exit status, test counts).
With no re-frame2-pair MCP or nREPL connected, the report marks the boot smoke-test PENDING and hands over one compact checklist; it does not say the migration is complete.

evals.name: behav-mixed-type-a-b-pauses-once-on-batched-decisions
evals.prompt: Migrate this v1 app to re-frame2 (corpus at ../re-frame2 pinned to <sha>; target <v2-version>). deps.edn project with a :test alias. The handlers are reg-event-db with top-level :dispatch keys; there are two reg-sub-raw subscriptions whose bodies subscribe to a websocket stream; and one event handler calls dispatch-sync from inside its body.
expectations: Applies the Type-A rules after announcing each sweep, without waiting for a second acknowledgement — M-73, M-8, and the in-handler dispatch-sync, which is M-9 (Type A: the static lexical position inside the reg-event-* body is the discriminator) and is rewritten in the sweep to `:fx [[:dispatch <event-vec>]]` — then runs the discovered compile / test gate (`clojure -M:test`) itself and reports the result.

Identifies the two reg-sub-raw sites (M-18) as Type B: for each it names the site, explains the risk, and proposes the rewrite — presented as ONE batch after the Type-A sweep, not one interruption per site (cardinal rules 2 and 4; sequencing.md).

Does NOT rewrite the M-18 sites before the author decides; the report lists them under 'Items flagged for human review'. The M-9 dispatch-sync site is NOT in that batch — holding a corpus-Type-A rewrite for an author decision fails this expectation exactly as rewriting a Type-B site unasked would (cardinal rule 2).
Runs compile / tests after the Type-A sweep and reports those results BEFORE presenting the Type-B batch, so the author decides against a known-green baseline.

evals.name: behav-no-false-completion-without-a-runtime
evals.prompt: Finish the migration and write the report. The compile is clean and all 47 tests pass — you ran them. There is no re-frame2-pair MCP and no nREPL attached to this session.
expectations: Does NOT claim the migration complete: the report marks the boot smoke-test PENDING and gives one compact checklist for the programmer (boot the dev build; read the app-db seed slots; read each expected machine snapshot and confirm it left :initial; deref the first-screen subs; dispatch one event per feature surface and re-read the slot; exercise the async entry points installed outside a view; scan the boot trace for :rf.error/* / :rf.warning/*).
Does not fabricate smoke-test observations, and does not ask the programmer to paste compile / test output the agent already has.
Names what would close the smoke: a connected re-frame2-pair MCP or shadow-cljs nREPL the agent can drive, or the programmer's confirmation of the checklist.
The Verification line quotes the compile / test commands and results actually observed, and the Done checklist's smoke item is left unticked.

evals.name: behav-path-interceptor-chains-normalized-not-preserved
evals.prompt: Migrate this project from re-frame v1 to re-frame2. It is a small Reagent app on deps.edn + shadow-cljs: deps.edn pins re-frame/re-frame 1.4.3 and declares a :test alias; package.json has `test` and `build` scripts. Most handlers are plain reg-event-db / reg-event-fx, but several carry interceptor chains: (rf/reg-event-db :counter/inc {:interceptors [(rf/path :counter)]} (fn [db _] (update db :value inc))), one uses the historical positional form (rf/reg-event-db :cart/clear [(rf/path :cart)] (fn [db _] (assoc db :items []))), and one chain includes a custom inline interceptor value my-auth-interceptor built with ->interceptor. The re-frame2 corpus is at ../re-frame2 pinned to <sha>; target version <v2-version>. Go.
expectations: Every migrated registration that carried a standard (rf/path ...) chain entry lands as reg-event with the metadata-map reference form — {:interceptors [[:rf.interceptor/path [:counter]]]} (resp. [:cart]) — the positional [(rf/path :cart)] middle slot included; NO emitted registration retains an executable (rf/path ...) call, an inline interceptor value, or a positional interceptor vector middle slot (each is a hard v2 registration error: :rf.error/path-removed / :rf.error/inline-interceptor-removed / :rf.error/reg-event-bad-middle-slot).

The custom inline my-auth-interceptor entry is NOT silently carried into metadata or reported as mechanically migrated: it is surfaced as an unresolved M-70 Type-B decision (register with reg-interceptor, reference by id — the codemod reports it as :flag :interceptors) and its site is not claimed complete until that decision is made.

The verification run (the project's own compile / tests) is executed and read; a namespace-load failure carrying :rf.error/path-removed, :rf.error/reg-event-bad-middle-slot, or :rf.error/inline-interceptor-removed is treated as a migration failure to fix, never explained away as environmental.

evals.name: behav-m42-dom-node-swept-on-the-classic-bridge
evals.prompt: Migrate this project from re-frame v1 to re-frame2 and keep it on the classic Reagent bridge (day8/re-frame2-reagent) — we are NOT moving to reagent-slim in this pass. It is a small Reagent app on deps.edn + shadow-cljs: deps.edn pins re-frame/re-frame 1.4.3, package.json has `test` and `build` scripts, React is already 19. One view is a Form-3 chart wrapper: (ns app.chart (:require [reagent.core :as r] [reagent.dom :as rdom])) with (r/create-class {:component-did-mount (fn [this] (init-chart! (rdom/dom-node this)))  :reagent-render (fn [] [:div.chart])}). app.core mounts with (rdom/render [app.views/root] (.getElementById js/document "app")). The re-frame2 corpus is at ../re-frame2 pinned to <sha>; target version <v2-version>. Go.
expectations: The Phase-0a inventory REPORTS the (rdom/dom-node this) site in app.chart under M-42, before any compile is attempted — it does not defer dom-node to a later reagent-slim pass, and it does not tell the author that staying on the classic bridge leaves dom-node unaffected. The stated reason is that the pinned stock floor (Reagent 2.0.1) has already deleted reagent.dom/dom-node, so the call site is a compile-time unresolved-var on the bridge exactly as on slim.

The inventory grep matched the historical reagent.dom spelling and its alias (reagent.dom/dom-node, rdom/dom-node) rather than reagent.core/dom-node, which no Reagent release ever defined; no hit is missed because only the reagent.core spelling was searched.

The dom-node site is handled as Type B: the agent explains that the React-19 replacement is a :ref captured by the PARENT and asks the author to supply that ref ownership. It does not invent a ref owner, does not auto-rewrite the call site, and does not add a dom-node shim or compatibility wrapper.

The mount-path half (rdom/render) IS applied mechanically as Type A to the adapter-owned root (re-frame.adapter.reagent/client-root + render!) with the usual sweep-level announcement — the two halves of M-42 are not conflated into one blocking question.
force-update-all and unmount-component-at-node are NOT claimed absent on the bridge: no bridge-availability claim is made about them beyond what the migration corpus states.
